rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient that spans nearly the full solvent-strength range at a moderate slope and temperature, to reveal how many compounds elute early, late, or only at high organic. This should place most or all compounds on-scale in one run and give a useful first map of the elution window for later trimming and optimization.

All pairs are already fully resolved, so the only score loss is the last peak at 12.64 min; the next step is to trim the gradient to the actual elution window and make it shorter to pull the last peak under 10 min while keeping adequate spacing. Based on the first run, the peaks span roughly phi_e about 0.11 to 0.41, so a 0.10-0.60 window with a 10 min gradient should keep all compounds in-gradient but substantially reduce t_last.

Resolution still has comfortable margin, and the score is now limited only by the last peak being slightly beyond 10 min, so push retention down modestly by shortening the gradient and raising temperature. This should move the last peak under 10 min while likely keeping the worst pair above 1.5.

The collapse of pair 6/7 at higher temperature shows this pair is temperature-sensitive, while injection 2 at the same window had adequate resolution but only a slight time penalty. Keep the beneficial higher temperature to shorten the run, but restore the gentler 10 min slope to recover resolution and test whether this combination lands both full resolution and t_last under 10 min.

Pair 6/7 is harmed mainly by the temperature increase, so return to 40 C where all pairs were resolved; to shave the remaining 0.58 min from the last peak, slightly lower phi1 to make the gradient shallower and better focused on the actual elution range. This should preserve or even improve the critical pair while potentially moving the late peak just under 10 min by keeping the whole sample more tightly inside the active gradient window.

Lowering phi1 made the late peak much worse, so the last compound needs a stronger final eluent, not a weaker one. Since the critical pair is fully safe at 40 C, test a slightly stronger and shorter gradient at the same temperature to pull the last peak below 10 min while watching whether pair 6/7 stays above 1.5.

The 8 min gradient was too steep and compressed the critical 6/7 pair, while higher temperature also hurts that pair, so move in the opposite direction on both variables: restore a gentler slope and lower temperature to improve selectivity. Using the stronger phi1 of 0.65 should still keep the last peak near or under 10 min while giving the best chance to recover full resolution.

The data suggest 40 C is the safest temperature and the main tradeoff is between the 10 min method with full resolution but slight time penalty and the 8 min method that may gain time at the cost of compressing the critical region. Test the direct missing point at the original 0.10-0.60 window, 8 min, 40 C to see whether it preserves enough resolution while bringing t_last below 10 min; if so it could beat injection 2.

Injection 8 is close to optimal on time, but the only remaining score loss is the 6/7 pair at R 1.18; lowering temperature may improve selectivity for that critical pair without sacrificing too much run time. This directly tests whether a small temperature drop can push the worst pair to 1.5 or better while keeping the last peak under 10 min.

At 40 C, reducing tG from 10 to 8 improved time enough to outweigh some loss in the critical pair, so the optimum likely lies between those slopes; with grid constraints, the only way to test the other side is a slightly longer gradient to see whether restoring full credit to pair 6/7 can outperform the small time penalty. This run will show whether higher resolution margin near the critical pair is worth the extra retention, or confirm that 8 min is already near-optimal.

Injection 8 is the best so far, and the main remaining deficit is only the 6/7 pair, so try shifting the gradient window slightly lower while keeping the winning slope and temperature. Lowering phi0 can redistribute the early-middle region and may improve selectivity around the critical cluster without sacrificing the strong enough phi1 that keeps the last peak under 10 min.

Shifting phi0 downward worsened the critical pair, so test the opposite direction from the current best method. Raising phi0 slightly while keeping the successful 8 min, 40 C conditions may alter selectivity in the crowded middle region enough to improve pair 6/7 while still keeping all peaks within a short run.

Raising phi0 from 0.10 to 0.15 improved both the CRF and the critical 6/7 pair while keeping the run short, so continue in that direction by one grid step. This tests whether a slightly higher starting organic further improves the crowded mid-run selectivity enough to reach full credit on the last unresolved pair without giving up the sub-10 min last peak.

The best region appears to be around phi0 0.15 at 8 min and 40 C, and increasing phi0 further was slightly worse; now test narrowing the upper end of the window by one step while keeping the successful lower bound. A slightly shallower gradient in the same time may improve the critical 6/7 separation enough to gain full credit, while t_last should still remain comfortably below 10 min.

You already have a perfect method, so any further run is only to probe whether a slightly narrower upper window can preserve full resolution while pulling the last peak a touch earlier. Lowering phi1 by one grid step keeps the successful phi0, tG, and temperature fixed while testing the closest plausible neighbor to the optimum.

You already have a perfect method, so the only sensible exploration is a nearby neighbor that might also score 1.000 while offering margin around the critical pair. Since lowering phi1 alone made the late peak too slow, combine that narrower upper window with a slightly higher phi0, which previously shortened the run, to test the closest adjacent window around the optimum.

You now have two perfect methods, and the newer one is slightly faster with the last peak at 9.82 min; a nearby higher-phi0 variant could retain full credit while moving the last peak a bit earlier. This is the closest unexplored neighbor in the successful region and tests whether additional upward shift of the window keeps the critical pair just above 1.5.

The upper edge at 0.55 works when phi0 is 0.20, but pushing phi0 to 0.25 caused the first pair to compress toward the dead-time region; the next useful boundary test is therefore to lower phi1 by one step while keeping the proven phi0 0.20. This probes whether a narrower 0.20-0.50 window can still keep the last peak under 10 min and maintain full resolution, or whether 0.20-0.55 is already the robust optimum.

You already have a perfect method at 0.20-0.55, 8 min, 40 C; the only remaining worthwhile question is whether a shorter gradient can keep all pairs at R>=1.5 while further reducing run time. This is the nearest faster variant of the proven optimum and directly tests the resolution margin of the critical 6/7 pair.

The 6 min gradient at phi0 0.20 compressed the critical 6/7 pair too much, so test whether lowering phi0 back to 0.15 restores enough selectivity while keeping the faster run. This is the shortest variant of the other perfect window and is the most informative remaining check near the optimum ridge.

With two perfect methods already found, remaining exploration is only about nearby robustness; the critical 6/7 pair sits just above 1.5 in the faster perfect method, so a small temperature decrease may increase separation margin while likely remaining under 10 min. This directly tests whether the successful 0.20-0.55 window is temperature-robust near the optimum.

The successful region is clearly centered at 40 C and an upper window of 0.55, while both shorter tG and lower T damaged the critical cluster. Test a slightly longer gradient at the faster perfect window to see whether it preserves full resolution with more margin and still stays under 10 min, potentially giving a more robust co-optimum.

Both perfect methods are at 40 C, but the only unexplored immediate neighbor in that successful window is a small temperature increase at the more conservative phi0 0.15 setting. This checks whether the stronger 6/7 resolution margin there can tolerate 45 C while perhaps giving a slightly faster co-optimum, though the expectation is mainly to confirm temperature sensitivity around the optimum.

With the optimum already secured, the only remaining value is mapping the nearby failure boundary on the fast side; 0.20-0.55 at 6 min lost the critical pair, so testing 0.20-0.60 at the same 6 min asks whether a slightly broader, stronger window can recover enough selectivity while keeping a very short run. This is the closest untested fast neighbor around the best phi0 region.

For the final run, map one last nearby fast-boundary condition by increasing phi0 one step from injection 24; this will show whether the very short 6 min regime can be made viable by shifting the window upward, or confirm that the best methods at 8 min are the true optimum. The campaign already secured CRF 1.000, so this last injection is best used to complete the local shape of the optimum region.
